# LEVIATH Frontier 0.1.0

An owned, deterministic island foundation for an isolated OpenMW candidate.
The plugin adds exactly sixteen exterior CELLs and sixteen LANDs. It contains
one own region, three own terrain materials and no original-world overrides.
The terrain is groundwork for exploration and a later central plaza; native
rendering, traversal, physics and entry remain pending the coordinated probe.

## Inputs and generated bytes

The bound Foundation profile resolves sixteen ESM/ESP inputs. The builder
checks the exact profile digest, content order, source-file digests, exterior
coordinates and own IDs before writing. A changed or colliding input stops
the build. It never writes an input, original save or global profile.

The new block covers `x=64..67`, `y=-64..-61`, with physical bounds
`X=[524288,557056]`, `Y=[-524288,-491520]`. The terrain uses one seeded
257x257 heightfield. Adjacent cells share the same 65x65 edge vertices;
heights are quantized once to eight world units. All outer-border heights
are -2048, matching OpenMW's default height for absent LAND.

The own 512x512 DXT1 ground, stone and coastal-soil textures include ten
mip levels. LAND uses only local palette values 1..3, which address own
LTEX indices 0..2. No Morrowind textures, meshes, LAND data or music are
copied. These simple procedural materials do not establish a modern visual
quality claim.

## Rebuild through Git Bash

Use an existing Python3.14 with Pillow12.3 and the exact bound Foundation
runtime's `esmtool.exe`. The Bash entry invokes the deterministic source
generator, the separate byte decoder, two identical builds and the existing
native file parser:

```bash
PYTHON='/c/Python314/python.exe' bash verify-frontier.sh \
  '<absolute-path-to-bound-foundation>/openmw.cfg' \
  '<absolute-path-to-bound-foundation>/runtime/esmtool.exe'
```

The source code accepts paths supplied by its caller. It does not download
packages or start OpenMW. `PARSER_BINDING.json` binds the existing parser's
bytes. Its report is `ESMTool version 1.3`, distinct from the OpenMW0.51
release containing it. This binary intentionally returns1 for `--version`;
the actual `dump` parsing command returns0 on the observed candidate.

## Additive candidate configuration

Append these two lines after the bound Foundation content in a separate
test profile, replacing the placeholder with the actual candidate path:

```ini
data="<absolute-path-to-presentation-candidate>/frontier-candidate/mod"
content=LEVIATH-Frontier.esp
```

`cfg-additive.txt` contains the same lines. Later mods or a different content
order require a fresh collision binding. There is no automatic teleport on
normal load, no portal script and no network listener in this terrain unit.

## Entry and coordinated native acceptance

`ENTRY.json` binds the generated ESP digest and the explicit entry:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Exterior name | `LEVIATH Frontier Entry` |
| Grid | `(65,-63)` |
| Player position | `(536576,-512000,576)` |
| Decoded terrain height | `320` |
| Initial vertical margin | `256` |
| Suggested initial rotation | `0` radians |
| Central pad centre | `(540672,-507904,320)` |
| Flat pad radius | `6200` world units |

The root fixture may use the documented player teleport API in a separate
profile. The new entry name resolves an exterior CELL. The initial margin
allows a short fall onto the pad; observed landing and ground clearance are
required before a travel feature calls this a safe arrival.

The next native probe should bind the same plugin/ENTRY hashes and observe:
successful material loading, a terrain ray hit at the entry, player landing,
movement across at least one shared CELL edge, a coastal material transition,
the sea boundary and a representative map/landscape screenshot. Preserve the
original save. A local portal is a separately versioned gameplay module.

## Observed verification and coverage

`CHECK_RECEIPT.json` records all sixteen decoded height codecs, 1,551 shared
vertex comparisons, 66,049 covered global vertices, 7,385 flat-pad vertices,
upward quantized normals, white colour continuity, DDS mip-chain lengths,
WNAM samples, VTEX permutation/palette closure and entry height. The same
check independently rescans all sixteen bound content files for coordinate
and own-ID collisions. Two asymmetric codec/palette oracles and two
deliberately mismatched weather writer contracts are checked.

`DETERMINISM_RECEIPT.json` records six byte-identical outputs across two
builds: ESP, three textures, ENTRY and the own heightfield preview. Receipt
timestamps are outside that equality claim. `ESMTOOL_RECEIPT.json` records
the existing native parser's accepted record schema. Its lazy LAND payload
handling does not validate rendering or physics; the independent serialized
decoder supplies the stated byte-level coverage.

## Exact weather/version coupling and sources

The authored HEDR version is float32 TES3_1.3, bytes `6666a63f`, whose stored
decimal value is `1.2999999523162842`. The own REGN WEAT has ten bytes and
probabilities Clear60/Cloudy30/Foggy10, totaling100. The
[OpenMW0.51 writer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMW/openmw/openmw-0.51.0/components/esm3/loadregn.cpp)
writes eight bytes specifically for VER_120 and ten otherwise. Its reader
also accepts either size under newer headers. Our checker enforces the
candidate's stricter writer convention; it does not label all readable
legacy region records invalid.

The source contracts are pinned by `PRIMARY_SOURCE_RECEIPT.json` and
`PRIMARY_MORE_RECEIPT.json`. Relevant primary implementations are
[LAND codecs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMW/openmw/openmw-0.51.0/components/esm3/loadland.cpp),
[CELL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMW/openmw/openmw-0.51.0/components/esm3/loadcell.cpp),
[LTEX](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMW/openmw/openmw-0.51.0/components/esm3/loadltex.cpp),
[LAND dimensions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMW/openmw/openmw-0.51.0/components/esm3/landrecorddata.hpp)
and [world-unit constants](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMW/openmw/openmw-0.51.0/components/misc/constants.hpp).
They were read for format semantics. Their GPL source bytes remain in the
bounded work folder and are not relabeled or redistributed as this own code.

Own code, generated terrain, textures and preview use the included MIT
license. `PLAN.md` preserves the earlier approved plan; current maturity is
the generated and statically verified candidate described above.
